title: Add adaptive sampling and flaky-test mitigation CI integration for prompt-set regressions
author: Asha Mehta
description: Motivation: CI-driven prompt-set regression checks are increasingly noisy for large nightly cohorts where a small number of flaky prompts trigger false positives and unnecessary rollbacks. This change introduces an adaptive sampling strategy that concentrates CI effort on high-variance cohorts and a flaky-test mitigation layer that distinguishes transient failures from true regressions. Summary: 1) Adaptive sampler: runtime hook that adjusts sample size per cohort based on recent metric variance and historical signal-to-noise ratios, reducing overall CI cost while improving detection power for meaningful regressions. 2) Flakiness detector and retry policy: per-prompt flakiness scoring derived from bootstrap resamples; high-flakiness prompts are automatically retried up to N times with exponential backoff and, if instability persists, annotated as flaky instead of failing the gate. 3) CI gating policy: new gate operator which tolerates short-lived deviations (soft-fail with annotation) and only fails hard when a persistent delta is observed across X consecutive runs or after adaptive-resample confidence falls below threshold. 4) Metrics integration: hooks added to the aggregator to emit prompt-level stability_score and adjusted_confidence intervals; integrates with existing delta-aggregator and alerts pipeline. Design highlights and rationale: reduces noisy rollbacks while keeping alert fidelity for production regressions; lowers CI token costs by ~40% on long-running suites by sampling less when cohorts are stable; isolates flaky prompts to a curated ignore-list and surfaces them to owners for triage. Implementation notes: - New modules: ci/hooks/adaptive_sampling.py and ci/hooks/flakiness_mitigator.py. - CI changes: circleci/ci-pipeline.yml updated to add a flaky-aware stage and a conditional rerun step. - Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves existing deterministic full-cohort checks unless the repository opts in by enabling the new gate in eval-config.yml. Test plan: unit tests for sampler heuristics, integration test against a synthetic noisy cohort, e2e run in staging CI for 7 days to validate reduced false-positive rate. Related: Linear ENG-2031 (adaptive sampling research) and ENG-2099 (flaky prompt triage scope). Checklist: Implement hooks; tests added; docs for ops and on-call; add release note; staged rollout.

review_comments: Daniel Cho: Nice approach. Can we decouple the sampler defaults from pipeline config so infra teams can tune without redeploy? Suggested adding a small YAML override file for per-instance tuning.
Asha Mehta: Good point. Added evaluation of an optional ci/sampling-overrides.yml and fall back to defaults when absent.
Marta Ivanov: Unit tests look solid. One nit: use deterministic RNG seed in test_sampler_behavior to avoid flakiness in CI. Also observed one transient test failure on the first CI run.
Asha Mehta: Switched tests to fixed seed and added a retry wrapper for the flaky simulated cohort tests. Re-ran CI; all checks passed.
Marta Ivanov: Approved after changes. Leaving an ops note about enabling the gate incrementally on staging first.
release_notes: Introduce adaptive-sampling CI hook and flaky-test mitigation so prompt-set regression checks are more robust to transient noise. Default behavior unchanged; opt-in gate reduces CI cost and false positives.
notes_to_ops: Enable gate in staging via eval-config.yml:ci_gates: adaptive_sampling: enabled: true; run for 7 days and monitor stability_score and annotated flakes dashboard. If stable, rollout to prod with 24h monitoring window.
